abstract_sentences.text: What do thinking language models learn during training that their base models lack?

evidence.anchor: What do thinking language models learn

abstract_sentences.text: We first present an unsupervised method that discovers a model’s reasoning behaviors by training small Sparse Autoencoders on sentence-level activations of reasoning traces, yielding interpretable reasoning taxonomies.

Building on this, we introduce constructive model diffing, which aims to reconstruct the base-to-fine-tuned difference from interpretable components: reasoning mechanisms (category vectors that can induce a reasoning behavior in the base model) and reasoning heuristics (a classifier determining when a mechanism should fire).

Across nine base/thinking pairs (four RL-trained, four SFT-distilled, one mixed), two independent findings agree: category vectors in the base model converge to far lower loss for taxonomies derived from purely RL-trained models, and hybrid models recover roughly 76% of the RL base-to-thinking gap but only 11% of the SFT gap.

This indicates RL primarily teaches heuristics for orchestrating pre-existing base mechanisms, whereas SFT-distillation installs new ones, offering a new lens on what training paradigms teach, with implications for efficient reasoning-model development.

experimental_design.name: research question and training-paradigm hypothesis
experimental_design.description: The paper asks what thinking models learn beyond their bases and tests an RL-heuristic versus SFT-mechanism interpretation.

evidence.anchor: What exactly do thinking models learn

experimental_design.name: nine model configurations
experimental_design.description: Four RL-trained ORZ pairs, four SFT-distilled DeepSeek-R1-Distill pairs, and one mixed QwQ pair from 0.5B to 32B.

experimental_design.name: taxonomy training data
experimental_design.description: MMLU-Pro supplies 12,102 prompts and 430,122 sentence activations across six distributed layers per model.

experimental_design.name: category-vector training mixture
experimental_design.description: 9,794 training questions and 995 validation questions from MATH, Natural Reasoning, SciBench, and TheoremQA.

experimental_design.name: evaluation data
experimental_design.description: GSM8K, MATH500, and a 1,000-question Hendrycks-MATH holdout are evaluated.

experimental_design.name: leakage control
experimental_design.description: MATH training is disjoint from MATH500; the Hendrycks holdout has zero shared problems with training mix and MATH500; model-set selection does not use evaluation benchmarks.

experimental_design.name: controls and prompting
experimental_design.description: Base, hybrid, and thinking models are compared; base and hybrid use identical minimal question-answer prompts.

experimental_design.name: decoding protocol
experimental_design.description: Base and hybrid decode greedily; thinking models sample three rollouts at temperature 0.6; all use a 2048-token budget.

experimental_design.name: training hyperparameters
experimental_design.description: SAE uses Top-K k=3, batch size 512, maximum 300 epochs, patience 10; vector/MLP optimization uses AdamW, separate 1e-2/1e-3 learning rates, batch 4, maximum 10 epochs.

experimental_design.name: randomness and selection
experimental_design.description: Three independent vector/MLP sets are trained per pair and the highest 788-question holdout-mix recovery is selected; ORZ-7B SAE stability uses five seeds.

experimental_design.name: scoring and human validation
experimental_design.description: Claude Sonnet 4.6 grades accuracy, three judge repetitions are used, and Appendix C reports Cohen kappa 0.880 against humans.

experimental_design.name: hardware
experimental_design.description: The paper names vLLM serving but provides no GPU model, hardware count, wall-clock budget, or compute-cost total.

experimental_design.name: pre-registration and predeclared failure criterion
experimental_design.description: No pre-registration statement or predeclared success/failure threshold was located in the full PDF.

experimental_design.name: implementation source
experimental_design.description: The introduction footnote links a public GitHub codebase and results repository.

result_inventory.claim: Low-dimensional SAE taxonomies are usable and stable for the selected configuration.
result_inventory.value: Figure 2 identifies an elbow at 10-20 categories; ORZ-7B five-seed stability is 93.3% matched and 0.886 mean cosine; 14/15 human labels fully or partially agree.
result_inventory.comparison: Grid-search configurations and five ORZ-7B seed runs; human versus LLM labels.
result_inventory.statistical_method: normalized metric grid; pairwise Hungarian cosine matching; exact category agreement counts.
result_inventory.adverse_explanation: Stability is measured only for one ORZ-7B SAE, so general stability across all models remains uncertain.

result_inventory.claim: ORZ-derived category vectors converge to lower held-out CE than R1-derived vectors.
result_inventory.value: Figure 3 reports lower curves for all three held-out sets; raw endpoint CE values are not tabulated.
result_inventory.comparison: RL-trained ORZ versus SFT-distilled R1, with mixed QwQ in between.
result_inventory.statistical_method: holdout cross-entropy by training epoch; best validation epoch marked.
result_inventory.adverse_explanation: The figure does not give a numeric endpoint table, so exact loss differences are uncertain.

result_inventory.claim: RL pairs recover much more of the base-to-thinking performance gap than SFT-distilled pairs.
result_inventory.value: The paper reports roughly 76% average recovery for four RL models versus roughly 11% for four SFT-distilled models.
result_inventory.comparison: Nine base/thinking pairs across GSM8K, MATH500, and held-out Hendrycks-MATH.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Accuracy mean plus/minus std over rollout-judge pairs; Rec.% is the gap fraction closed.
result_inventory.adverse_explanation: The authors state lower SFT recovery could reflect genuine mechanism change or limits of vector optimization.

result_inventory.claim: Larger SFT bases recover more than smaller SFT bases, while size-matched ORZ remains higher.
result_inventory.value: R1-Distill-14B/32B have positive recovery on all listed benchmarks; the small distilled pairs are near zero or negative; ORZ-32B exceeds R1-Distill-32B and QwQ-32B in Table 1.
result_inventory.comparison: Size trends within distilled models and 32B comparisons.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Per-pair benchmark Rec.% with accuracy mean plus/minus std.
result_inventory.adverse_explanation: This is not a controlled training-algorithm comparison because published model families can differ beyond training method.

result_inventory.claim: High-recovery RL hybrids use sparse steering.
result_inventory.value: ORZ rows steer about 5-12% of generated tokens across three benchmarks.
result_inventory.comparison: RL rows compared with 12-24% for most distilled/mixed rows.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Per-problem mean steering fraction; Table 5 adds mean plus/minus std.
result_inventory.adverse_explanation: Sparsity alone cannot rule out every output-bias alternative; the paper adds negative-control ablations.

result_inventory.claim: Each constructed-diff component matters in the tested RL pairs.
result_inventory.value: Figure 4 reports full 77/77 recovery, random-category 20/28, random-vector -28/-13, MLP-only -8/-1, and random-position -8/28 for ORZ-1.5B/32B.
result_inventory.comparison: Full pipeline versus four negative controls on averaged GSM8K and MATH500.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Gap recovered percentage averaged across two benchmarks.
result_inventory.adverse_explanation: Random positions retain 28% at ORZ-32B, so position gating is not the only useful component there.

result_inventory.claim: A qualitative trace exhibits self-verification under hybrid steering.
result_inventory.value: The Qwen2.5-32B/ORZ-32B hybrid steers about 12% of positions across six categories, reaches answer 17, and the unsteered base fails in the displayed MATH500 example.
result_inventory.comparison: One hybrid trace versus its unsteered base trace.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Qualitative case study; no distributional statistic.
result_inventory.adverse_explanation: It is a representative single case, not a randomly sampled effect estimate.

claim_closure.claim: An unsupervised SAE method discovers interpretable reasoning behaviors.
claim_closure.method_response: Sections 2.1-2.3 define SAE clustering, LLM labels, and three taxonomy metrics.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 2, Table 3, and Appendix C give selection, stability, and one human validation.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion does not independently restate the taxonomy evidence.

claim_closure.claim: Constructive model diffing can explicitly reconstruct a useful base-to-thinking difference.
claim_closure.method_response: Sections 3.2-3.6 build category vectors, a heuristic, and hybrid generation.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 1 reports recovery; Table 2/Figure 4 test sparse intervention and components.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Section 6 restates the framework and two components.

claim_closure.claim: RL-trained and SFT-distilled thinking models learn fundamentally different things.
claim_closure.method_response: The same diffing pipeline is applied to four RL, four SFT, and one mixed pair.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 3, Table 1, scale trend, and Figure 4 support an RL/SFT performance-recovery contrast.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Section 6 repeats the RL average recovery and lower SFT recovery.

claim_closure.claim: Sparse steering rules out the hypothesis that the hybrid simply biases specific outputs.
claim_closure.method_response: Disagreement gating and category vectors limit intervention to selected positions.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 2 shows 5-12% ORZ steering and Figure 4 removes several meaningful components.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: No separate conclusion paragraph returns to this alternative.

final_judgment.single_storyline: Constructive model diffing operationalizes the base-to-thinking difference as mechanisms that exist in the base and a heuristic for when to deploy them; high sparse hybrid recovery supports the authors' RL heuristic interpretation, while SFT's lower recovery supplies the contrast.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The main body keeps the what/when diagram, taxonomy grid, CE comparison, Table 1 absolute and recovery results, Table 2 sparsity, Figure 4 controls, and three limitations.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Appendices hold SAE/LLM evaluation prompts, human validation, split and optimization details, vector usage, one trace, and nine full taxonomies. The main body is adequate for a decision on the headline result but not for a full reproducibility or label-quality audit.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 1 defines the two components, Table 1 joins absolute accuracy to gap recovery, and Figure 4 dismantles the construct component by component.
final_judgment.largest_gap: The RL-versus-SFT explanation is only partially identified because pairs differ beyond training method and the paper explicitly preserves a category-vector-optimization alternative; Appendix G also imposes a substantial audit burden.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For a claim about what fine-tuning learns, construct an executable hybrid, report absolute performance plus recovery and intervention sparsity, then use component-wise negative controls.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: Recovery establishes functional adequacy of a proposed decomposition, not its uniqueness or a fully isolated training-algorithm cause when model family, data, teacher, and optimization can co-vary.
